subsystems.name: Crop growth chamber
subsystems.role: grows edible plants that simultaneously fix carbon dioxide, release oxygen and produce food.
parts: sealed growth racks with pressure and humidity control

subsystems.name: Air revitalisation loop
subsystems.role: keeps oxygen and carbon dioxide within safe limits by cycling gases between crew, plants and machines.
parts: Sabatier reactor to make methane and water from CO2 and hydrogen

subsystems.name: Algae or photobioreactor
subsystems.role: a compact, high-rate gas exchanger that also yields protein-rich biomass.

subsystems.name: Water recovery loop
subsystems.role: reclaims urine, condensate and grey water back to potable standard.
parts: ion exchange and activated carbon beds

subsystems.name: Waste and nutrient recycling
subsystems.role: returns plant residue, packaging and human waste to usable plant nutrients.
parts: nutrient dosing into the hydroponic solution

subsystems.name: Environmental control and monitoring
subsystems.role: holds temperature, humidity, pressure and light cycles steady and tracks the loop mass balance.
parts: sensor suite (O2, CO2, humidity, trace gases)

buildSteps.title: Fix the loop mass balance
buildSteps.detail: Work out how much oxygen, water and food each crew member needs per day — of the order of a kilogram of oxygen and a few kilograms of water — then size every loop so nothing accumulates or runs short over months.

buildSteps.title: Build sealed growth chambers
buildSteps.detail: Assemble pressure-tight racks with LED arrays delivering the high light levels crops need, plus hydroponic channels and root-zone irrigation.

buildSteps.title: Select the crop mix
buildSteps.detail: Choose species that combine high edible yield, quick harvest, and easy processing — wheat, soy, potato, sweet potato and leafy greens are the usual candidates — and stagger planting so harvests overlap.

buildSteps.title: Install the air loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect CO2 scrubbers, a Sabatier reactor and an electrolyser to the plant chambers so carbon moves from crew to plants to food and back, with buffers for night-time when plants stop photosynthesising.

buildSteps.title: Build the water loop
buildSteps.detail: Add urine processing, condensate collection and polishing beds, with sampling to confirm water meets drinking standards.

buildSteps.title: Close the solid-waste loop
buildSteps.detail: Feed inedible plant mass and human waste through biological or chemical oxidation to recover nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium for the nutrient solution.

buildSteps.title: Integrate control and monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Link all loops to a model of the whole system so operators can see where mass is accumulating and respond to failures such as a contaminated crop or a stalled bioreactor.

buildSteps.title: Test with a crew in a sealed analog
buildSteps.detail: Run multi-month closed-chamber trials with people inside, measuring how much resupply mass is actually avoided and where the loops leak.

prerequisites.why: crops need far more light than sunlight-free habitats can supply any other way, and waste heat must be rejected.
the ISS already recycles water and generates oxygen chemically, providing the machinery the biological loops are built around.

prerequisites.tech: Reliable plant growth in reduced gravity
prerequisites.why: plants do grow in orbit, but yield, seed-to-seed cycles and root-zone behaviour under microgravity and partial gravity are still being proven.

prerequisites.tech: Stable, safe microbial and bioreactor systems
prerequisites.why: biological reactors must run for years without drifting into unusable or hazardous states.
crops grown in recycled waste streams must be verifiably safe and palatable enough that crews actually eat them.

pathway.milestone: small plant-growth facilities on orbit and closed ground chambers such as ESA's MELiSSA work and Russia's BIOS-3 experiments
pathway.unlocks: data on crop yields, gas exchange rates and crew interaction with plant systems.

pathway.milestone: multi-loop ground demonstration with a crew sealed in for months to a year
pathway.unlocks: evidence that air, water and food loops can be integrated and controlled together.

pathway.milestone: plant modules attached to a lunar surface habitat
pathway.unlocks: partial closure of life support where resupply is expensive, plus experience with reduced gravity and dust.

pathway.milestone: transit and surface habitats with high loop closure
pathway.unlocks: crewed missions far from Earth, where resupply mass is the binding constraint.
